functions.does: The black gear on the roof steers the front wheels: its upright shaft and a pair of bevel gears turn a long shaft forward under the cabin to the pinion on the front steering rack.
functions.source: book: page 180 (top left photo, the arrow on the front wheel) and page 181 (the roof gear marked); the steering's build steps are inferred

functions.does: Pushed along, the rear wheels drive the V6 engine behind the seats: the rear differential's ring gear turns a 20 tooth gear that drives the crankshaft through a 12 tooth gear, and the six pistons run up and down; the half shafts reach the sprung rear wheels through constant velocity joints.
functions.source: book: rear axle and engine build steps; page 181 (top right photo shows the engine under the lifted rear body); which steps is inferred

functions.does: The front wheels roll freely; only the rear ones are driven.
functions.source: inferred: the front axle has no drive shaft

functions.does: All four wheels have independent suspension: each hub rides on a pair of arms with a stiff yellow shock absorber, so each wheel can rise and fall on its own.
functions.source: book: page 181 (top middle photo, the arrows on the rear wheels)
functions.note: the springs only matter under the car's weight; each wheel's travel is what's checked

functions.does: The bonnet lifts up at its back edge, hinged at the front.
functions.source: book: page 180 (bottom left photo, the arrow on the bonnet)
book: page 180 (bottom left photo) and page 181 (top right photo), the arrows on the doors

functions.does: The rear of the body, with the rear roof, rear wings and spoiler, tilts up from the back to show the engine and rear suspension; the engine and rear axle stay on the chassis.
functions.source: book: step 257 (the yellow arrows on the rear body), page 181 (top right photo, the arrows on the rear body)
